Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — burst shape + commit sizing

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — InsightAI is excited about Redwood Dedicated for our inference stack. Before we lock a reserved commitment, procurement needs a clearer sizing artifact that maps our burst/baseline traffic to a proposed reserved footprint and a failover plan.

Quick ask: can you send a short questionnaire or template that captures (1) token-level burst profiles, (2) expected concurrency per endpoint, (3) average prompt/response lengths by route, and (4) acceptable p99 latency targets by workload? We have an upcoming exec review next Thursday so a tight turnaround would help.

Attached is a small CSV export of our observed 14-day request histogram (insightai_burst_profile.csv) and a one-pager with example prompts (prompt_sample_response_lengths.pdf).

Cheers,
Tara Singh
Head of ML Products
InsightAI

Tara — thanks for the files and the quick follow-up. Looping in Marissa (pre-sales capacity) and Ben (solutions) so we can turn this into a concise sizing recommendation for your exec review.

At a high level, we'll need the following from you to map to a reserved commit + burst plan: 
- Representative 7/14/30-day rolling period (you sent 14d, perfect)
- Distinct routes/endpoints and percent traffic split (chat vs. embeddings vs. classification)
- Prompt tokens (median/p90) and response tokens (median/p90) per route
- Desired p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs per route
- Whether any endpoints require data residency or private deploy constraints

I'll attach a short questionnaire below as a form you can paste answers into. Once we have numbers, Ben will run a burst-to-GPU mapping (including KV cache assumptions and batching headroom) and we can propose a Reserved Capacity + Burst Pool configuration.

Action items:
- Tara: paste the route-by-route metrics into the questionnaire by EOD Fri PT
- Marissa/Ben: we will synthesize a recommended commit and an optional overlay plan for <10% latency degradation during sustained bursts

Thanks — we should be able to get a draft doc for your review by Monday.

--
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@insightai.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — burst shape + commit sizing

Tara — thanks for the detail, this is great. I pulled the CSV and ran a quick mapping using our standard assumptions: 
- Model: rdx-large-v2 (quantized fp16 path) for chat/classify; embedding model: rdx-embed-1
- KV cache retention: per-session with average 30-token prefix reuse for chat (saves ~18% token compute in steady state)
- Batching headroom: we assume continuous batching reduces per-token latency cost by ~12% at 8–12 concurrent requests per GPU for chat-like workloads

Preliminary recommendation (high level):
- Committed footprint: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent (zone us-west) — this covers baseline sustained load (~60% of typical day) with room for horizontal autoscale to handle mid-sized bursts.
- Dedicated burst pool: reserve an additional 4 x A100-80GB equivalent that can be used for short 10–20 minute peaks. This pool uses our fast pre-warm policy so median cold-start is <45s for model weights.
- Fallback plan: when burst pool saturates, route non-critical classify/embedding traffic to lower-cost variant (rdx-classify-small, rdx-embed-slim) with graceful degradation. Chat routes remain on committed capacity with reduced concurrency caps to protect p99 targets.

Estimated observable outcomes:
- Expected p99 for customer-chat: ~430ms (meets 450ms target) under recommended commit+burst allocation for 95th percentile observed bursts.
- Embeddings p99: ~180ms
- Classify p99: ~270ms

Next steps:
1) Marissa — I'll hand this to you for a two-slide exec summary (one slide commit + burst mapping, one slide failover + cost delta).
2) Tara — if this looks reasonable, we'll convert to a formal quote and map contract term for the reservation.

Notes/assumptions: numbers above assume 20% write-through cache hit for repeated prompts and a conservative batching efficiency. If InsightAI can accept slightly relaxed p99 (e.g., 500ms), we can reduce committed footprint by ~1 GPU.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
